execution_order: fixed by §7.4, restated with what each step means against the consumers actually found
steps: 1 inventory every consumer — done by this Map and MACHINE-CONSUMERS.json; no entry may be rewritten before its consumers are listed

2 freeze the new authority schema and the single write point — registry.yaml subset plus generated-write.mjs GENERATED_FILES are the existing surfaces; extending GENERATED_FILES is the only sanctioned widening

3 deploy double-READ diagnostics, no double-write — the existing double-reader is checkLegacyMirror (LEGACY_MIRROR_INCOMPLETE / LEGACY_MIRROR_VALUE / LEGACY_MIRROR_SCHEMA_MISMATCH); it reads graph and the derived mirror and never writes graph

4 switch consumers one by one to a versioned authority snapshot, machine readers first (census-runtime.yml awk, then ci-pr-gate checkCurrentContract, then gen-current-state, then doc-checks, then docs-probe)

5 real CI negative controls for old/new conflict, missing field, unknown id and forged C1/C2 — the existing control set is packages/testkit/test/a5-current-contract.test.ts (P1-P3, N1-N5) and scripts/doc-consistency-controls.mjs; its inline fixture currently carries only 3 of the 6 fields and must be widened first, otherwise the negatives it cannot express will silently pass
6 switch the current pointer in a single transaction (six fields + current_phase + every repointed reader in one commit)

7 verify the derived mirror is read-only and cannot reverse-decide authority (LEGACY_MIRROR_VALUE proves mismatch only while the graph block exists; after the switch a dedicated refusal is required, since checkLegacyMirror reads the graph block it no longer holds)
8 rehearse the inverse migration before claiming reversibility
no_double_read_note: double-read is allowed only through the existing mirror check; no second reader may become a decision maker. docs:probe declares its own limits (T0 only, no C1/C2/C3 substitution, cannot replace a ci-pr-gate leg) and those limits stay true after migration.

rollback.anchor: pre-migration recorded SHA and pointer snapshot, taken from git (the commit that precedes the switch) plus the verbatim six-field block, not from dev/engineering/current-state.json
rollback.prohibition: §7.4 forbids recovering authority from a derived mirror such as current-state.json; current-state.json can be deleted and regenerated, it can never be a source
rollback.required_proof: rollback itself must pass the CI negative controls and an independent review, and must be rehearsed in step 8 before the switch is claimed reversible
rollback.note: graph.yaml is git-tracked so the textual revert is trivial; the non-trivial half is that a reader left repointed at the new authority would keep reading the new location after a text revert, which is why readers move in the same commit in both directions

gaps_found_this_round: G1 census-runtime.yml:129 parses current_contract.baseline with its own awk expression: a second independent definition of the pointer grammar outside ci-pr-gate, not covered by a5-current-contract fixtures. A migration that changes block shape breaks the hosted job, not the local leg.

G2 checkCurrentContract reads and grades all six fields, but info.contract carries only phase_id, active_plan, baseline and baseline_collected (scripts/ci-pr-gate.mjs:313): the backlog and matrix PATHS are consumed internally (Q2 existence, GROUP C id population, Q5 row contract, Q6 reference lines) and then not surfaced. Any step-3 double-read built on info.contract therefore sees 4 of 6 values and needs the two paths added, or it will report coverage it does not have.
G3 doc-consistency-controls.mjs:63-68 fixture graph carries 3 of 6 fields, so part of the required negative space is currently unprovable.

G4 registry.yaml:9 migration_of_legacy_consumers is already recorded as not_started_requires_coordination and is mirrored into the derived view, but no machine reader gates on that value; it is documentation-shaped state today.

G5 the sentence that makes the legacy block the authority until an approved migration is REQ-EB-0003 (docs/contracts/engineering-baseline/ids.yaml:105-108, mirrored into INDEX.md:150-155) and its normative_status is proposed-not-ratified; the contract that authorises the switch is itself unratified. Ratifying the 18 IDs is outside this round.

G6 docs-probe reads authority only through the derived-view mirror (scripts/docs-probe.mjs:128 viewMirror) and uses only phase_id; a new authority without a mirror would leave the probe blind rather than red.

G7 no writer of graph.yaml exists in scripts/ (verified: no fs write call names graph.yaml in scripts/); the write point is a human commit guarded by dev/agent-workflow/hooks/pre-commit YAML-parse check. Any "single write point" claim must describe a human-commit discipline, not a tool.

G8 docs/contracts/engineering-baseline/plan-citation-interface.md:40 cites INV-EB-0012 as the basis of PLAN_CITATION_CONFLICT, but ids.yaml declares only INV-EB-0001..INV-EB-0010 — INV-EB-0012 is declared nowhere in the tree (verified by git grep at the fixed ref, single hit: that citation itself). The concept C-EB-0012 does exist (docs/glossary.md:22) and carries the same substance, so this reads as a mis-keyed id rather than a missing rule. No existing checker catches it: the id-resolution checks (verify-agent-notes note-reference rules, registry REGISTRY_REF_UNRESOLVED) cover note frontmatter and registry refs, not prose inside contract documents. Migration step 5 should add that coverage, because a rule whose cited id does not resolve is exactly a rule that can quietly stop being true.
